images.title: Filling one whole circle
images.purpose: Show the one idea the student practises: fractional unit pieces of different sizes fill one whole, and a running sum in a common unit tells how much is still empty.
images.composition: One large circle on the left with wide space around it, and a short column of two equation lines on the right.
images.exact_structure: Left: one large flat circle, the whole, with a dark outline. A teal #0072B2 sector fills exactly one half of the circle (180 degrees). An amber #E69F00 sector fills exactly one fourth (90 degrees), next to it. The remaining one fourth (90 degrees) is empty, outlined with a reddish purple #CC79A7 dashed line. Thin grey #6B7280 lines mark the sector edges from the centre. Right: two equation lines stacked with wide spacing. Exactly 1 circle, 3 sectors: 1 teal, 1 amber, 1 empty.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any app control or screen interface drawn in the frame
images.takeaway: Add the pieces in one unit to see what is left.
images.description: A circle with a teal half and an amber fourth placed; in fourths, 1/2 + 1/4 = 3/4, so one fourth of the circle is still empty.
images.context: Shown with the doer concept before the student practises. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to say how much of the circle is filled, in fourths, and how much is still empty.

image_decisions.why: Pieces filling a circle with a running sum is a picture idea; one clean circle primes the puzzle without giving any puzzle answer.
